title: Happy Young Women, Grumpy Old Men? Emotion-Driven Demographic Biases in Synthetic Face Generation
abstract: arXiv:2602.00032v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Synthetic faces from text-to-image (T2I) models pervade digital media, yet their demographic biases under emotionally conditioned prompts remain poorly understood. We aim to systematically audit how emotionally conditioned prompts affect demographic and perceived-attractiveness biases in synthetic faces generated by T2I models, with particular attention to intersectional patterns and cross-ecosystem differences across model families. We audited eight (4 Western and 4 Chinese) T2I models and generated 56,000 faces under seven prompt conditions: a neutral baseline and six emotion conditions. We quantified biases in gender, race, age, and perceived attractiveness using information-theoretic divergence metrics. We further conducted intersectional analyses across combined demographic attributes and compared patterns between the Western and Chinese model groups to assess cross-ecosystem consistency and divergence in bias behavior. translated_title: 快乐的年轻女性，暴躁的老年男性？合成人脸生成中情绪驱动的人口统计偏差
translated_abstract: 来自文本到图像（T2I）模型的合成人脸遍布数字媒体，然而它们在情绪条件提示下所呈现的人口统计偏差仍然鲜为人知。我们旨在系统地审计情绪条件提示如何影响T2I模型生成的合成人脸中的人口统计和感知吸引力偏差，特别关注交叉性模式以及不同模型家族之间的跨生态系统差异。我们审计了八个T2I模型（4个西方模型和4个中国模型），并在七种提示条件下生成了56,000张人脸：包括一个中性基线和六种情绪条件。我们使用信息论散度度量量化了性别、种族、年龄和感知吸引力方面的偏差。我们进一步对组合的人口统计属性进行了交叉性分析，并比较了西方和中国模型组之间的偏差模式，以评估偏差行为在跨生态系统上的一致性与分歧。
tldr: 本研究系统审计了8个西方和中国的文生图模型在情绪条件提示下生成的56,000张合成人脸，揭示了情绪提示会驱动人口统计偏差（如年轻女性更易被生成为快乐形象、老年男性更易被生成为暴躁形象），并通过信息论指标量化了性别、种族、年龄和感知吸引力方面的交叉性偏差及东西方模型生态系统的差异。
en_tdlr: This study systematically audits 56,000 synthetic faces generated by 8 Western and Chinese T2I models under emotion-conditioned prompts, revealing emotion-driven demographic biases (e.g., happy young women, grumpy old men) and quantifying intersectional biases in gender, race, age, and perceived attractiveness across model ecosystems using information-theoretic divergence metrics.
